title: Concurrency, lifecycle, cancellation, and shutdown
purpose: Find races, deadlocks, leaks, use-after-close behavior, shutdown corruption, and background-work ownership bugs across Ledger runtime components.
invariants: Cancellation and shutdown must not leave authoritative mutations half-applied or acknowledged incorrectly.
Every long-lived goroutine must have a bounded ownership/lifecycle and a reliable termination path.
Channels, queues, workers, stores, and transports must not be used after their owning component is closed.
Shutdown ordering must respect dependencies between admission, consensus/apply, persistence, projections, transport, and serving layers.
Concurrent start/stop/error paths must not deadlock or double-close shared resources.
Context cancellation must propagate without converting committed work into an inconsistent local rollback.
Background work must not outlive the generation/configuration/state that authorized it.
Races must not change deterministic FSM/business outcomes.
adversarial_questions: Which goroutines can block forever if a downstream consumer exits first?
Where can close/cancel race with send, receive, flush, apply, snapshot, or retry?
Can shutdown acknowledge completion before durable/background work has actually stopped?
Can a worker from an old generation mutate state after restart/reconfiguration?
Are errors during startup unwound in strict reverse ownership order?
Can multiple error paths close the same channel/store/transport?
Can context cancellation interrupt an operation after an irreversible side effect but before bookkeeping?
Do tests rely on sleeps that hide races or fail to reach the intended concurrent state?
